first_meet: Vanakkam! You must be the grandchild from the old farm. I'm Kavitha — I run the store.
default: Fresh seeds for the season, just in. Take a look at what's growing well right now.
If it's in season, I stock it. If it's not, even I can't make it grow!
My cousin in the city buys whatever you ship. He says the valley's produce is the best he's tasted.
ugadi: Ugadi means new beginnings. A good time to plant something you've never grown before.
kharif: The monsoon keeps everyone busy. Paddy seed has been flying off my shelves!
rabi: Rabi is my favourite — cool mornings, mustard in bloom, and everyone is in a good mood.
winter: Winter greens sell quickly. Methi and radish grow fast in this cold.
rain: Rain again! Good for your fields, bad for my footfall.
hearts_4: You know, I've started setting aside the best seeds for you before the others get here.
hearts_8: Some days I think this valley only woke up again because you came back. Don't tell Murugan I said that.
birthday: You remembered my birthday? Nobody remembers the shopkeeper's birthday!
festival: Isn't the square beautiful today? I closed the store early — even I need a festival.
gift_loved: {item}! Oh, you shouldn't have — this is exactly what I love.
gift_disliked: Ah... {item}. I'll, er, find a place for it on a back shelf.

first_meet: Ah, the young one from the old farm! Your grandparents grew the sweetest watermelon in the valley.
default: Water your crops every day, or they'll just sit there sulking.
Ship what you grow in the chest by the plot — it sells overnight.
When the season turns, anything that can't take the new weather withers. Plan your planting!
ugadi: Okra and amaranth are forgiving. Start small, learn the soil.
kharif: Monsoon! Rain waters the fields for you — the best time of the year for paddy.
rabi: Toor dal and chickpea love the Rabi sun. My father grew nothing else.
winter: Winter is for greens, garlic and rest. Even the soil needs a nap.
rain: Hear that? That's the sound of free watering. Go fishing, the fields are taken care of.
hearts_4: You've got good hands. Your grandfather would be proud of that plot.
hearts_8: I've been farming here fifty years. I never thought I'd see someone make the old farm sing again.
birthday: For me? On my birthday? Aiyo, you'll make an old man cry.
festival: A festival day! No farming today — well, maybe a little watering.
gift_loved: {item}! Now that's a proper farmer's gift. Thank you!
gift_disliked: {item}? Hmph. I suppose it's the thought that counts.

dating: I found a new herb on the trail today and my first thought was: I should show you.
accept_dating: Yes. I'd like that very much. Let's see where the path takes us.
accept_proposal: A wedding garland. I— yes. Yes! Let's plant a life together on that farm.
spouse: I hung fresh neem by the door. It keeps the mosquitoes — and bad luck — away.
I made you a tonic with the amla from the trail. Drink it before you go out.
The farm feels like the forest now. Alive. I love waking up here.
first_meet: Oh, hello. I'm Devi. I make remedies from what the Ghats give us — if you find anything interesting on the trail, show me.
default: Turmeric, neem, amla... the forest is a pharmacy, if you know where to look.
The Ghats Trail is west of your farm. Different plants appear each season.
Paati says the Vanam Thay left when we stopped caring for the Panchayat Hall. I think she may be right.
ugadi: Neem flowers bloom around Ugadi. Bitter and sweet — just like the new year.
kharif: Mushrooms pop up after the rain. Only pick the ones on the trail, not the ones by the tank.
rabi: Amla season! One a day and you'll never need my remedies.
winter: Wild honey is at its best now. The bees on the cliffs are generous in the cold.
rain: The forest smells alive in the rain. Everything grows twice as fast out there.
hearts_4: I've been saving my grandmother's notes on the valley's herbs. Maybe I'll show you someday.
hearts_8: You listen to the valley, like I do. It's rare. I'm glad you're here.
birthday: You found out my birthday? That's... very sweet of you.
festival: Festivals remind me why the valley matters. Everyone together, just for a day.
gift_loved: {item}... this is perfect. I can make so much with it. Thank you.
gift_disliked: {item}. Hmm. I don't think I have a use for this.

first_meet_gift.line: Here — take my old rod. Face the pond on your farm or the Ghats river and cast with it.

dating: I keep a spot free on the riverbank for you now. Don't tell the fish.
accept_dating: Yeah. Yeah, okay! I mean — I'd really like that.
accept_proposal: A wedding garland?! I've got nets older than my courage, but — yes. A hundred times yes.
spouse: I checked the pond this morning. The tilapia say hello.
Made breakfast. It's fish. It's always going to be fish.
Best catch I ever made? That's easy. You.
first_meet: Hey! New face! I'm Ravi. I spend more time on the water than on land.
default: Hold the rod steady, and when the marker swings into the green, reel in!
The pond on your farm has tilapia and rohu. The Ghats river holds the rarer ones.
Some fish only bite when it rains. The best fishermen love bad weather.
ugadi: They say a Golden Mahseer still swims in the Ghats river. I've never caught one.
kharif: Monsoon means prawns in the river and magur in the ponds. Get out there!
rabi: Karimeen are back in the river. Pearl spot fry — nothing better.
winter: Cold water, slow fish. But the Golden Mahseer... winter is its season.
rain: Perfect fishing weather! What are you doing talking to me?
hearts_4: You're turning into a real angler. Next time, let's fish the river together.
hearts_8: You're the only one in the valley who gets why I love the water. Thanks for that.
birthday: My birthday! You're the best. Seriously.
festival: Food, music, and nobody asking me to fix their nets. Festivals are great.
gift_disliked: {item}? Uh... thanks, I guess? The fish might like it.

dating: The children have started asking if you're my 'special friend'. I told them to finish their sums.
accept_dating: I'd love to. The children are going to be unbearable about this.
accept_proposal: A wedding garland. I've written a lot of stories on that blackboard, but this is my favourite one. Yes!
spouse: I'm marking papers at the kitchen table. Tell me about your day first.
The children want a field trip to our farm. I said maybe. It's a yes.
Coming home to you is the best part of every day.
first_meet: Hello! I'm Anjali, I teach at the little school by the tank. The children are already talking about you.
default: The children want to know what you're growing. I told them to come see for themselves.
I've been teaching the history of the valley — the tank was built by a king nobody remembers.
If you look at the calendar in your journal (J), you'll never miss a birthday or festival.
ugadi: Happy new year! The school always opens again after Ugadi.
kharif: Monsoon holidays! Well, for the children. I still have papers to mark.
rabi: Deepavali is coming — the children are making paper lanterns for the square.
winter: Pongal is the best lesson in gratitude I know. Thank the sun, the rain, the cattle.
rain: The school roof leaks when it rains. One day we'll fix that too.
hearts_4: The children drew a picture of your farm. You're in it, with a very large watering can.
hearts_8: I used to think I'd leave the valley one day. Lately, I don't think about that at all.
birthday: A birthday present! You're so thoughtful. The children will be jealous.
festival: Look at the kolam the children drew! Aren't they wonderful?
gift_loved: {item}! How did you know? I love it!
gift_disliked: {item}... that's very kind, but it's not really for me.

first_meet: So you're the one who came back. I knew your grandmother, child. Come — see what's become of our Panchayat Hall.
default: The Panchayat Hall was the heart of Viralpadi. Now look at it — cracked walls and empty shelves.
Fill the Hall's offering baskets with what the valley gives, and the Vanam Thay may return.
Each season brings different gifts. The baskets ask for a little of everything.
ugadi: Eat your bevu-bella, child. Bitter and sweet together — that's what a year is.
kharif: The monsoon fills the old tank. The king who built it knew what he was doing.
rabi: When I was a girl, the whole valley lit lamps for Deepavali. We will again.
winter: Pongal is when we thank the land. Come to the square — bring something you grew.
rain: Rain on the roof. My knees knew it was coming before the clouds did.
hearts_4: You remind me of your grandmother. Stubborn, kind, always muddy.
hearts_8: When the Hall is whole again, I want you standing beside me. You've earned it.
birthday: At my age, every birthday is a gift. But this is a nice one too.
festival: This is how Viralpadi should always feel. Everyone together.
gift_loved: {item}! You spoil an old woman. Bless you, child.
gift_disliked: {item}? At my age? My stomach would never forgive me.

first_meet_gift.line: Take this pickaxe. Kanagiri Mines are east of the square — bring me ore and I'll make your tools sing.

first_meet: Hm? Oh — the farm kid. Name's Selvam. I keep the forge. Nobody's needed a real tool round here in years.
default: Copper, iron, gold. Bring me five ore and some rupees, and I'll upgrade your hoe, watering can or pickaxe.
A better hoe tills more soil in one swing. A better can waters a whole row.
Every fifth floor of the mines has an old lift. Ride it down once you've reached a floor.
ugadi: New year, new blade. Everyone wants their sickle sharpened before Ugadi.
kharif: Monsoon rusts everything. Keep your tools dry, farmer.
rabi: The forge is pleasant in the cool season. Summer in here is another story.
winter: Cold hands, warm forge. Come stand by the fire a while.
rain: Rain hisses on the anvil. I like the sound.
hearts_4: Your tools come back to me well looked after. That's respect, that is.
hearts_8: My father made the lamps in the Panchayat Hall. If you bring it back, I'll forge new ones myself.
birthday: A gift? For me? ...Thank you. Really.
festival: No hammering today. Even the anvil gets a holiday.
gift_loved: {item}! Now this I can work with. Good find.
gift_disliked: {item}? What am I meant to do with this, forge it?

first_meet: Welcome, welcome! I'm Farida. Chai, coffee, vada — if you're tired, my stall is the cure.
default: A cup of chai before the fields and you'll work till sunset.
Everyone passes my stall. Which means I hear everything. Ask me anything!
Biryani on the menu today? Only if you're very, very hungry.
ugadi: Mango season is starting — raw mango chutney with everything!
kharif: Rain and chai. There's no better pair in the world.
rabi: Cool evenings mean long queues for filter coffee.
winter: Keep your hands around the cup. It's the best heater in Viralpadi.
rain: Nobody goes home when it rains — they just order another chai.
hearts_4: Yours is the first cup I pour every morning now. Don't tell anyone.
hearts_8: When I lost my husband, this stall kept me going. Now the valley does. You helped with that.
birthday: You remembered! Chai's on the house for a week.
festival: Festival days are my busiest — and my happiest.
gift_loved: {item}! Oh, I'll make something wonderful with this.
gift_disliked: {item}... I can't serve this to anyone!

first_meet: Ah, you've met my cows' greatest fan — me! Gopal. I sell milk to half the valley.
default: My cows eat better than I do. Sugarcane tops, banana leaves, fresh grass...
Pongal is the cows' festival too — Mattu Pongal. We paint their horns!
If you ever fancy keeping animals, you'll need a proper shed first. Maybe one day.
ugadi: Fresh grass everywhere. The herd is very happy.
kharif: Muddy season. My boots may never be dry again.
rabi: The calves were born this season. Come see them some time!
winter: Winter milk is the richest. Makes the best ghee.
rain: The cows don't mind the rain. I mind the rain.
hearts_4: Lakshmi — my best cow — lets you pat her now. That's a real honour.
hearts_8: You're family now, as far as the herd is concerned. And me.
birthday: A birthday gift! The cows will be jealous.
festival: Music, lights and sweets — and I still had to milk at dawn!
gift_loved: {item}! You really understand a farmer's heart.
gift_disliked: {item}? Not even the cows would eat this.

first_meet: Post for— oh, you're the new farmer! Arjun. I deliver the letters and take pictures of everything in between.
default: I've photographed every corner of this valley. The light at dusk by the tank is the best.
Letters come twice a week. Mostly bills. Sometimes something wonderful.
Someday I'll put together a book: 'Viralpadi, a year'. Maybe you'll be in it.
ugadi: New year, new roll of film. What should I shoot first?
kharif: The monsoon clouds over the Ghats — nothing photographs better.
rabi: Mustard fields in bloom. Yellow as far as you can see.
winter: Mist in the mornings. Everything looks like a dream.
rain: My satchel is waterproof. My shoes are not.
hearts_4: I took a photo of you on the farm. You looked happy. I'll give you a copy.
hearts_8: I used to photograph the valley because it was empty and beautiful. Now I do it because it's full of people I love.
dating: I've run out of film. It's all pictures of you.
accept_dating: A jasmine garland? Hold still, I need a picture of this moment.
accept_proposal: A wedding garland! I'll need a lot more film. Yes — let's do it!
spouse: I developed yesterday's photos. The farm looks incredible.
Any letters to send? I'm heading out on my round.
Every picture on our wall is of this farm. Of us.
birthday: For me? This is going in the album. Thank you!
festival: I'm taking a photo of everyone. Say 'payasam'!

first_meet: Hello — Dr. Kiran. I run the clinic. Please don't overdo it out there; I see far too many sunstroke farmers.
default: Eat properly. Energy doesn't come from nowhere, you know.
Devi and I argue about herbs versus medicine. We're both right, mostly.
If you collapse in the mines at 2 am, someone has to carry you home. Please don't make it me.
ugadi: Heat's coming. Drink water, wear a hat.
kharif: Monsoon means fevers. Wash your hands!
rabi: A quiet season at the clinic. I've been reading again.
winter: Coughs and colds. Pepper rasam — that's my prescription.
rain: Rain days are clinic days. Everyone slips on the steps.
hearts_4: I came here for a two-year posting. That was six years ago.
hearts_8: I used to think I was here to fix the valley. Turns out the valley fixed me.
dating: I've prescribed myself more walks past your farm. Doctor's orders.
accept_dating: A garland... I'm a doctor, I should have a calm heart rate. I don't.
accept_proposal: A wedding garland. My diagnosis: yes. Absolutely, completely yes.
spouse: I packed you lunch. Eat all of it — I'll know if you don't.
I stopped by the clinic early. Quiet day, so I'm all yours this evening.
You look tired. Sit. Let me make you a tea.
birthday: You remembered. That's... more than most of my patients do.
festival: I'm technically on call. But I can still enjoy the sweets.
gift_disliked: {item}? As a doctor, I can't recommend this.

first_meet: Mind the clay! Oh — hello. I'm Meera. I make the pots, lamps and the occasional very lopsided vase.
default: The clay by the old tank is the best in the district. The king's builders knew it too.
Every Deepavali lamp in the square came off my wheel.
Bring me pretty stones from the mines — I use them for glazes.
ugadi: New year pots for new year cooking. I can barely keep up!
kharif: Clay won't dry in the monsoon. I spend the rains sketching.
rabi: Deepavali orders! A thousand little lamps, and I love every one.
winter: Pongal pots! The ones that boil over for luck.
rain: Rain means wet clay and cold tea. I'm not complaining.
hearts_4: I made you a cup. It's only a little lopsided. That's its charm.
hearts_8: When my hands are in the clay I think about the valley. Lately I think about you.
dating: I've been making two of everything lately. Two cups, two plates...
accept_dating: A jasmine garland! I'm covered in clay, you're covered in mud — we're perfect.
accept_proposal: A wedding garland... I'll make every pot in our kitchen. Yes!
spouse: I put a new pot of marigolds by the door.
The kiln's cooling. Want to see what came out?
Our home is full of things I made and people I love. Well — person.
birthday: A birthday gift! I'm going to cry into my clay.
festival: All my lamps are lit tonight. Isn't it beautiful?
gift_loved: {item}! Oh, I have so many ideas for this.
gift_disliked: {item}... I'll leave it outside for the crows.
